title: Nullish coalescing ??
description: Nullish coalescing ?? returns the right side ONLY when the left is null or undefined — NOT on 0, "", or false.

notes: ?? fires ONLY for null and undefined. || fires for ANY falsy value (0, "", false, NaN) — a frequent source of bugs.
Use ?? for defaults when 0, "", or false are valid values; use || when any falsy input should be replaced.
?? cannot be combined with || or && without parentheses — JavaScript forces you to be explicit.

options: false — `??` coerces the left operand to boolean first
true — short-circuit returns the first truthy operand
true — `||` returns a boolean, not the operand

questions.q: Which values cause ?? to use the right-hand side?

Whichever is longer — `??` picks the more-defined operand

exercises.prompt: Show ?? preserving 0 and "" but replacing null.

L3.prompt: Write `withDefault(v)` returning v unless v is null or undefined (then "missing"). Log `withDefault(0)`, `withDefault(null)`, `withDefault(undefined)`, `withDefault("hi")`.
